source: Met Office UKV (UK deterministic 2 km, mosg__model_configuration uk_det) from the Source Cooperative Icechunk archive or the Met Office open-data bucket, regridded at fetch onto a regular 0.02-degree latitude/longitude grid by woof.ukv_source, with the same-hour ERA5 (or, past ERA5's last published hour, GFS) land state and sea ice carried in band

licence.ukv: Met Office, British Crown copyright; the archive as distributed by Source Cooperative (source.coop/bkr/metoffice), the live runs by the Met Office on AWS Open Data (registry.opendata.aws/met-office-uk-deterministic); attribute the Met Office
licence.era5: Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) ERA5, read from Google's analysis-ready copy; 'contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information'
licence.gfs: NOAA NCEP GFS, read from the noaa-gfs-bdp-pds AWS mirror; United States government work with no copyright restriction

front_doors.archive: s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/bkr/metoffice/metoffice_uk_deterministic_2km.icechunk (Icechunk format 1, anonymous, branch main); the dated _29092024/_16052025 siblings are format 2 and are not read
front_doors.live: s3://met-office-atmospheric-model-data/uk-deterministic-2km/<RUN YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>/<VALID YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-PT<HHHH>H00M-<field>.nc (eu-west-2, anonymous, a rolling two years, oldest run 20241016T2200Z when listed 2026-10-18)

store_choice: a window inside the archive that avoids its missing hour is read from the archive (each hour's own T+0); any other window is read from ONE live run whose leads hold every valid time, the newest such run that has posted every object it needs

archive.time: time is int64 milliseconds since 1970-01-01, hourly, 14183 records 2024-01-01T00Z..2025-08-13T22Z with no gaps (MEASURED 2026-10-18); the store publishes no forecast_reference_time or forecast_period variable
archive.identity: each archive hour is the T+0 of that hour's run: the 2025-06-01T00Z archive hour equals the live 20250601T0000Z PT0000 objects to float16 rounding (300 hPa temperature max 0.0625 K, direction max 0.125 degree), while the 21Z T+3 and 23Z T+1 of the same valid time differ by up to 4 K (MEASURED 2026-10-18)
archive.precision: every published field except surface_air_pressure, air_pressure_at_sea_level and visibility is float16: temperature steps 0.125 K below 256 K and 0.25 K above, geopotential height steps 16 m above 16384 m (about 100 hPa and up); used as published
archive.wind_direction_gap: the pressure-level wind_from_direction array has 14182 records against 14183 times: the 2025-05-16T15Z record is absent and every later record is stored one index early (bisected against the height-level winds, and confirmed against the live T+0 of 2025-06-01T00Z, MEASURED 2026-10-18); later hours read index - 1, and a window holding that hour is served live or refused

live.objects: one NetCDF-4 object per field per lead, float32 on the same 2 km plane with scalar time, forecast_reference_time and forecast_period; the pressure-level objects store the 33 levels bottom first (100000..1000 Pa) and carry a status_flag for below-surface levels, whose values are present (no missing values MEASURED on the 20261016T0300Z run); the fetch checks units, plane, valid time, run and ladder of every object it reads
live.ladders: every UTC hour runs; 03Z and 15Z publish hourly to T+54 then three-hourly to T+120, 00/06/09/12/18/21Z hourly to T+54, the other hours hourly to T+12 (MEASURED from the bucket's listings of the 2026-10-12..18 runs)
live.fields: temperature, geopotential_height, relative_humidity, wind_speed and wind_direction on pressure levels; pressure_at_surface; temperature_at_surface; temperature and relative_humidity at screen level (height 1.5 m); wind_speed and wind_direction at 10 m; snow_depth_water_equivalent; height_of_orography

grid: UK 2 km standard grid: Lambert azimuthal equal-area on the WGS84 ellipsoid (semi-axes 6378137 / 6356752.314140356 m), origin 54.9N 2.5W, false easting/northing 0; 1042 x 970 cell centres, x -1158000..924000 m and y -1036000..902000 m at 2000 m; identical in both stores
wind_direction_frame: wind_from_direction (pressure levels and 10 m) is relative to TRUE north: the angle between the published 300 hPa direction and the geostrophic direction computed on the plane, regressed on the grid convergence over five dates, had slope -0.24 under the true-north reading and -1.24 under the grid-north reading (MEASURED 2026-10-18); components are earth-relative with no rotation

fetch_transform.crop: the requested area plus a 0.25-degree margin, on a regular 0.02-degree grid whose points are multiples of 0.02 degrees; every point must project inside the plane or the fetch refuses naming the first one outside
fetch_transform.horizontal: bilinear in projection metres from the four surrounding UKV cell centres
fetch_transform.winds: u = -speed sin(dir), v = -speed cos(dir) on the native grid, then interpolated as components
fetch_transform.terrain_height: live: the run's published height_of_orography (surface_altitude), the model's own surface under its surface pressure; archive (no orography published): the hypsometric height of the window's FIRST hour's surface pressure on that hour's pressure-level heights (first level above the ground, layer-mean virtual temperature between it and the 1.5 m screen state); either way one field written identically into every file, so the files are their own invariant terrain supplement
fetch_transform.screen_level: the 1.5 m screen temperature and relative humidity, used as published in the 2 m slots (declared screen_height_m 1.5)
fetch_transform.land_state: ERA5 when Google's ARCO copy (https://storage.googleapis.com/gcp-public-data-arco-era5/ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3, bounds from its .zattrs valid_time_stop_era5t) holds the whole window: land_sea_mask, sea_ice_cover and the four soil layers at the SAME valid time, layer-mean remapped from 0-7/7-28/28-100/100-289 cm to Noah's 0-10/10-40/40-100/100-200 cm, negative soil water (down to -0.01 over the sea) floored at 0 and counted; otherwise GFS 0.25-degree LAND, ICEC and the TSOIL/SOILW Noah layers from the GFS cycle at or before the live run (lead = valid - cycle, past f120 the posted three-hourly lead at or before it), byte ranges of the noaa-gfs-bdp-pds pgrb2.0p25 objects read through their .idx; both copied by nearest index (axis by axis, longitude modulo 360, ties to the lower index) onto the 0.02-degree grid, so nothing is interpolated and the borrowed coastline is the 0.25-degree donor's; GFS soil is missing over water and ERA5 sea ice over land, written as NaN-filled missing values
fetch_transform.why_in_band: a cross-source field_sources binding decodes its donor through the donor's own COMPLETE initialization mapping, and neither land-state product is fetched here as one: the fetch performs the same nearest-index borrow itself and records the product in every file's land_state_source attribute and the fetch manifest

soil: the files carry Noah's four layers, so the composition's conservative layer-mean remap is the identity; ocean soil is repaired after horizontal interpolation from skin temperature and unit moisture
model_top: the ladder reaches 1000 Pa (10 hPa, about 31 km); nothing above it is published, so the route has no upward extension

deliberate_exclusions.vertical_velocity: not published on pressure levels; the validated explicit zero
deliberate_exclusions.hydrometeors: cloud fractions and precipitation rates are diagnostics, not mixing ratios; the validated explicit zero
deliberate_exclusions.height_levels: the 5 m..6 km height-level fields are not read: the pressure ladder covers the whole column

input_identity: dynamic file paths and SHA-256 values are owned by gpuwm-mapped-composition-inputs-v1; the store, Icechunk snapshot or live run, and land-state objects each file was read from are in its source attribute and the fetch manifest
qualification: Implementation route, not an unchanged-stock-WRF certification
